title: Rescue Agent Task Package
description: The bounded scope package the director hands to a one-shot Rescue Agent after an implementer has failed the same task twice and the failure was classified as reasoning_gap or model_capability_gap. See RESCUE-PROTOCOL.md. Not a standing role — one task, at most two attempts.

failed_task_id.description: The original task_id, unmodified by hindsight.

failure_classification.description: Only these two classifications route to a Rescue Agent. diagnosis_gap, requirement_conflict, environment_issue, and rollback_needed never do — see RESCUE-PROTOCOL.md Step 1.

attempt_1.description: What the first failed attempt actually changed.

attempt_1_result.description: Verbatim evidence of the first attempt's outcome — test output or error, not a paraphrase.

attempt_2.description: What the second failed attempt actually changed.

attempt_2_result.description: Verbatim evidence of the second attempt's outcome.

confirmed_facts.description: What is actually established, with evidence, across both attempts.

last_passing_checkpoint.description: The commit, tag, or green-test state immediately before the first failed attempt. The Rescue Agent works from here, isolated (branch/worktree) where the platform supports it — not from the failed implementer's working state.

forbidden_scope.description: What the Rescue Agent may NOT do — e.g. redesign unrelated modules, change shared contracts not implicated by this failure. The Rescue Agent does not redesign the project; it receives only this failed task.

assigned_model.description: The director's explicit choice of a stronger model. Never automatic.

assigned_effort.description: The director's explicit choice of a higher reasoning tier. Never automatic.

max_attempts.description: Fixed at 2. Tracked separately from the implementer's own failure-loop count in FAILURE-LOOP.md.

attempt_number.description: Which Rescue Agent attempt this is (1 or 2).
